Twentieth Sunday in Ordinary Time August 16 2026 Welcome to Fr Theodore Ekwem who is with us through Sunday August 23rd During this time I am away on an informal sabbatical to complete my licentiate thesis through the Catholic University of America special Thank you to Fr Theodore for being with us on campus during this time For any parish needs please contact the Parish Office This weekend August 15th 16th the Church celebrates the Twentieth Sunday in Ordinary Time Our Gospel presents us with one of the most shocking encounters in Jesus public ministry Canaanite woman approaches Jesus pleading that He heal her daughter Though Jesus initial response seems difficult to understand He draws out something remarkable from her a faith so persistent and humble that it becomes an example for all who follow Him This Gospel continues our theme of discipleship Last Sunday we heard how the storms of life can reveal how fully we keep our eyes on and trust in the Lord This Sunday we discover that true faith does not give up simply because God may seem silent or because His answers to our prayers are not done in the timeframe we want Authentic faith perseveres continuing to seek Him out even if and when His plans unfold differently than our own Our first and second readings help to reveal just how shocking the Gospel encounter with the Canaanite woman an outside and Gentile truly was Isaiah saw a day when Gentiles would be welcomed into relationship with the Lord and God's house would become a house of prayer for all peoples Israel had been chosen by God but not merely for its own sake through Israel God intended to draw every nation to Himself Yet Israel struggled to accept this St Paul himself a Pharisee wrestles with this mystery as he watches Gentiles receive the Gospel even as many of his own people struggle to accept it Though this may sound reasonable to us it truly was a revolutionary idea in Jesus day God's saving mercy going beyond Israel and every other boundary including nationality culture and even our own expectations of God Israel had to learn that their understanding of what they wanted God's plan to be was not God's full plan His plan is so much larger than what we can imagine The Canaanite woman stands as living proof that faith may be found where no one expects it True discipleship sometimes requires us to surrender not only our own plans but even our assumptions about what God is planning practical challenge this week Whenever you are tempted to stop praying because nothing seems to be changing pray even more Like the Canaanite woman trust in God and refuse to let discouragement have the final word Basic Evangelization Training Pope St John Paul II famously declared Now is the time to commit all of the Churchs energy to a New Evangelization But many are left wondering What does that actually look like On Saturday Aug 22nd we will host St Paul Street Evangelization's Basic Evangelization Training one of the most practical and engaging evangelization workshops available today Whether you are hoping to better share Christ with your children or grandchildren invite a neighbor back to Mass accompany a coworker or simply become more comfortable speaking about our Faith this workshop is for you It will help to equip you with practical methods and tools that can be used in everyday life to confidently share our Faith with joy and charity Jesus final command to the Church was to go and make disciples If youve ever wanted to be more confident in living that mission this workshop is for you Registration is free
